supported_claims: Trim studs engage threaded valve holes, not wood.
Different stem adapters and screws are provided.
Inner plate flat at wall; foam covers opening; outer drain downward.
Wrong adapter length can prevent engagement or cover seating.
Finished wall lies 2-7/16 to 3-3/4 inches forward of the indicated shower-outlet centerline.
Upper bare stem tip is nominally 3-1/2 inches forward of that same axis.
Use plaster guard MIN-MAX depth and secure piping to framing.
Rear backing is configuration-dependent and may not fit in 2x4 framing.
Valve-body or temperature-spindle leakage calls for seal/cartridge diagnosis.

upper_stem_screen.method: Subtract labeled inch dimensions; do not scale the drawing. Compare to existing AXIS-UPPER-TIP in original-wall frame.
upper_stem_screen.result: CONDITIONAL DEPTH FLAG; NOT AN ACCEPTED PHYSICAL FAILURE
conditions: The scan landmark must be the same bare upper stem tip, without a removable adapter.
Actual installed valve revision must match the nominal drawing.
Scan scale and tip reconstruction remain uncalibrated.
No numerical lower-stem diagnosis is inferred from this upper-stem dimension.

assessment.stud_rear_support: The valve threads retain the trim studs. The rear ends do not require wood anchorage; actual through-hole/rear travel must be inspected.
assessment.cut_or_drill: No selection. First verify same studs, wood contact, usable valve threads, and whether the wood is structural framing or added blocking. The inspected guides do not authorize stud cutting or a particular wood recess.
assessment.handle_depth: A wrong removable adapter can affect engagement/seating even with correct body rough-in. Correcting studs alone cannot establish handle fit.
assessment.water_paths: Internal supply/valve leakage and exterior water passing behind improperly seated trim are different checks. Bare stem projection alone is not a leak diagnosis.
assessment.new_backing_plate: Any added stack changes trim/adapter depth and adds a sealing interface; it is not automatically an approved remedy for shallow rough-in.

next_evidence: Identify the exposed upper and lower stem parts and available numbered adapters.
Check finished tile against the correct plaster guard, or measure the documented rough-in datum.
Read both actual stud projections and inspect their rear contact and retained thread engagement.
Dry-fit the final complete stack without forcing: original foam/inner plate, cover, adapters and handles; verify seating, operation and drainage.
